predecessors.note: Dinuzulu's grant of 16 August 1884 (the page's lead); the infobox and body date the republic's formation to 5 August 1884. The Zululand dossier (af-07-a) records the matching loss in August 1884.

successors.note: Incorporated 20 July 1888 'on its own request'; the republic kept considerable autonomy. Britain's Natal took the territory from the Transvaal in 1903 (see colony-of-natal).

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 10,205 km2 shape (lon 31.7-32.8E, lat 28.1-26.8S, east of Swaziland in the Lubombo country) is not where the page puts the republic: it shares no cell with a 40 km circle at Vryheid (30.8E), the capital, whereas the page's 13,600 km2 (no year given; ratio 0.75) fits a 66 km circle at Vryheid. The same mislocated polygon is what Cliopatria adds to the South African Republic in 1890. Use the Vryheid region for 1884-1888 (the shape's own years 1885-1889 overshoot the 20 July 1888 incorporation).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the republic's real years and place: formed August 1884 around Vryheid, incorporated into the Transvaal 20 July 1888. The 1887 British annexation of 'a stretch of the republic's coastline' (the Mhlatuze mouth to St Lucia Bay, which the surveying committees had added) is not drawn: the page dates neither the extension nor its size.

region.text: the north-west of Zululand around Vryheid, the capital; the 66 km radius reproduces the page's 13,600 km2 (the same region the Zululand dossier uses for its 1884 loss)

ledger.note: 1884: the Boers form the Nieuwe Republiek at Vryheid. 'On 5 August 1884 the Boers formed the Nieuwe Republiek (New Republic)'; on 16 August 1884 Dinuzulu issued a proclamation granting 1,355,000 morgen of Zulu territory (the page's lead dates the independence proclamation to 16 August; the infobox says 5 August). The page gives the grant in morgen and the capital, not a boundary: the region is a 66 km circle at Vryheid sized to the page's 13,600 km2.

region.text: the coastal stretch from the Mhlatuze River mouth to St Lucia Bay

ledger.note: 1887: Britain annexes the republic's coast. 'During 1887, the British annexed a stretch of the republic's coastline and the Zulu Kingdom north of the Thukela River, to deny the republic sea access' (surveying committees had extended the border to the sea, from the Mhlatuze River mouth to St Lucia Bay). The coordinates are the two places; the page does not date the extension, so no keyframe draws the strip.

region.text: the north-west of Zululand around Vryheid, the capital; the 66 km radius reproduces the page's 13,600 km2 (the same region the Zululand dossier uses for its 1884 loss)

ledger.note: 20 July 1888: the New Republic joins the Transvaal. 'On 20 July 1888 the New Republic was incorporated with the Transvaal Republic on its own request' (the republic kept considerable autonomy; the page's lead adds that residents feared British annexation after the June 1888 Zulu revolt was suppressed). The South African Republic page gives the same date.

wars.name: Zulu civil war of 1884 (Tshaneni)
wars.outcome: Dinuzulu and the Boers defeated Zibhebhu at Tshaneni on 5 June 1884; two months later the Boers formed the Nieuwe Republiek on the land Dinuzulu granted them.
wars.note: The Battle of Tshaneni took place on 5 June 1884 (100 Boers and 7,000 Zulu against Zibhebhu). The fighting is the republic's origin, not a territorial contest between two states, so no zone is drawn; the Zululand dossier (af-07-a) carries the 1884 loss.

certainty.note: The boundary is a grant of 1,355,000 morgen allotted by lottery in farms of 1,000-3,000 morgen; the page gives no boundary line, and the extension to the coast was never settled before Britain annexed it in 1887.

sources.title: Nieuwe Republiek
sources.note: Identity, 5/16 August 1884, area 13,600 km2, recognition 22 October 1886, 1887 coastal annexation, incorporation 20 July 1888, capital Vryheid, president Meyer, transfer to Natal in 1903.

notes: One page opened (budget 1-2). Settled: the republic's years (5 or 16 August 1884 to 20 July 1888), its capital and president, the 13,600 km2 area. Not settled: (1) Cliopatria's shape (1885-1889, 10,205 km2) sits in the Lubombo country east of Swaziland, not at Vryheid; the verdict is wrong and the correction is a 66 km circle at Vryheid, as in the Zululand dossier. Cliopatria's South African Republic row adds the same mislocated polygon in 1890 (two years after the real incorporation of 20 July 1888); see south-african-republic. (2) The page dates the founding both 5 August and 16 August 1884; the ledger uses August. (3) Britain recognised the republic on 22 October 1886 (page), Germany, the Transvaal and Portugal earlier; recognition changes no border, so it has no event. (4) 'Utrecht' and the other districts that Natal received in 1903 are not named by this page (it says only that 'the territory was transferred to the British colony of Natal in 1903'); colony-of-natal carries that gain from the Colony of Natal page. (5) The coastal strip the page mentions is an event (1887 loss) without a keyframe. Gazetteer: none needed; all regions use Vryheid, which exists.
